paper_title: Constraints on Axion-like Particles from a Hard $X$-ray Observation of Betelgeuse
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis of Fig. 3
notes: First hard X-ray (NuSTAR, 50 ks) observation of Betelgeuse used to search for ALP-photon conversion in the Galactic magnetic field. 95% C.L. limits range from g_agamma < 5.2e-12 GeV^-1 (m_a < 5.5e-11 eV; optimistic: tcc=3.6 yr, BT=3.0 uG) to g_agamma < 1.8e-11 GeV^-1 (m_a < 3.5e-11 eV; conservative: tcc=1.55e5 yr, BT=0.4 uG). Emitted points encode the CONSERVATIVE mass-independent limit as a flat line over the low-mass validity range (lower edge 1e-14 eV taken from the paper's exclusion plot range). Limit degrades at higher masses (Fig. 3/S7) but numerical values there are only available from plots. Not a dark-matter halo search, so no local DM density assumed.
